- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or mildly negative over recent days; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp price spikes, leading to premature declines in forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates the true price, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements in the first 5–7 days, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Avoid overreacting to recent sentiment extremes; model often overweights sentiment in the first 3–5 days of forecast, then underweights it later.
- When sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, model should reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior period, unless price is trending upward.
- For price spikes >10% from recent mean, model should apply a 15–20% downward adjustment in the next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
